scope.purpose: Let the user enter one calendar date in a form, by typing it in a segmented field or by choosing it in a calendar opened beside the field.
useCases: An appointment or a deadline, chosen in the calendar near today.
A date of birth, typed in the segments.
A date bounded by min and max (no date in the past, no date beyond a year).
Composed with a TimeInput for a date and a time.
exclusions: A range of dates (DateRangePicker, later), several dates, several months shown at once.
A time in the same field (compose a TimeInput).
Arbitrary unavailable dates (weekends, booked days): out of v1 (user, 2026-11-23); min and max only.
Month and year lists in the calendar; non-Gregorian calendars; pasting a whole date.
A size option for the calendar panel: it follows density only (user, 2026-11-23, as for Table).
alternatives: InputText for a free-form date text the application parses (not recommended).
Three Selects (day, month, year) when the platform lacks a picker (not recommended).

decisionsTaken: Values are ISO strings where a date or time is involved; @internationalized/date (a peer dependency of Bits UI) is declared as a peer dependency of the package and used internally only (User in the Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_0156c545WiY1DREDPLwwFQEf (2026-11-23), wave 6 scoping, T1: "Ok pour moi, les dates font partie de ces choses difficiles à traiter sans dépendance externe").

Locale is a prop (BCP 47, default "en"), deterministic on the server; no application-wide locale provider: components are delivered as units with settings only, each project integrates its global logic (User in the Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_0156c545WiY1DREDPLwwFQEf (2026-11-23), wave 6 scoping, T2).

Segment names come from Intl.DisplayNames(locale, dateTimeField) and button labels are props with English defaults, replacing the English strings hard-coded in Bits UI (contract over Bits UI; User in the Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_0156c545WiY1DREDPLwwFQEf (2026-11-23), wave 6 scoping, T3).

Invalid belongs to the application: min and max limit the controls but never set invalid by themselves (User in the Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_0156c545WiY1DREDPLwwFQEf (2026-11-23), wave 6 scoping, T5).

Size sm, md, lg like InputText and Select, for the field only; the calendar panel has no size option and follows density only; its inner buttons are IconButtons sm (User in the Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_0156c545WiY1DREDPLwwFQEf (2026-11-23), wave 6 scoping, T4: "pas d'option de tailles pour la popover du datepicker [...] on peut partir sur des sm à l'intérieur").

Built on Bits UI DatePicker.Root, its segments and DatePicker.Calendar, inside a native popover from lib/overlay instead of DatePicker.Content (which is a Bits UI Popover with a portal, excluded by the overlay decision of 2026-10-31); DatePicker.Calendar only reads the root context (bits-ui 2.19.3, date-picker-calendar.svelte).

The calendar button is an internal part, not an IconButton: in an sm field (32 px) the smallest IconButton (32 px) does not fit inside the border. Its box is the new semantic role size.control.nested.{size} (one step below the field: 24, 32, 40 px in standard), the same box as the IconButton InputText places in md and lg fields.

Days outside the displayed month leave their cells empty and the grid always has six rows, so the panel keeps its block size; cells have the pitch of size.target.min (44 px) for the decision's minimum target, days a round box of size.control.sm.
Selected day in color.choice.on.* (a chosen value, like a checked Checkbox); other days in color.item.*; today marked by a ring in color.item.indicator.
The week starts on the first day of the week of the locale (Intl.Locale weekInfo), Monday when the platform does not expose it; Bits UI defaults to Sunday whatever the locale.

The calendar stays a popover in v1; on small screens it will open in a Drawer (bottom sheet) once that component is defined (user at the implementation gate, 2026-11-25: "ok pour la popover en v1 avec amélioration en drawer plus tard"). Recorded in authoring/component-catalog.md.

The calendar is rendered before it is first shown (pointer over or focus in the field, or opened by the application) so that it never appears empty; coalesced toggle events (close and reopen, or open and close, in one task) are reported locally.

A complete date typed before min or after max becomes the nearest bound when focus leaves the parts (instead of being kept); a value set by the application is not changed. (User in the Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_0156c545WiY1DREDPLwwFQEf, 2026-11-25: "Je n'avais pas compris ça du tout pour le datepicker désolé. Bien sûr qu'il faut pouvoir borner et qu'une date saisie hors borne se rapproche de la borne la plus proche. Donc la 2 aussi pour le TimeInput").

implementationNotes: Built on bits-ui 2.19.3 DatePicker.Root, DatePicker.Input with its segments, and DatePicker.Calendar with its grid, inside a native auto popover placed by lib/overlay floating (the button toggles it with popovertarget, which spares it from light dismiss); DatePicker.Content (a Bits UI Popover with a portal) is not used. Pinned version; each completion below is covered by a browser or SSR test (decision Contract versus Bits UI):

- Segments: aria-labelledby (the Field label or a hidden span holding the label prop, then a hidden span holding the part name from Intl.DisplayNames) replaces the English aria-label; an empty part has no aria-valuenow or aria-valuetext (Bits UI says "Empty"); the first part is described by the Field description instead of Bits UI's hidden "Selected Date:" element; aria-invalid follows the invalid prop only (Bits UI marks a date outside min..max invalid, also on the separators).
- Backspace empties the whole part: Bits UI removes one digit at a time; its handler runs as many times as needed, intermediate dates are not emitted.
- Parts written with Latin digits by Bits UI (the year in ar-EG) are shown in the locale's digits.

- Grid keyboard handled before Bits UI (whose keys are the arrows, Enter and Space, ignoring the reading direction): Page Up/Down, Shift+Page Up/Down, Home/End and right-to-left arrows; focus is clamped to min..max and waits for the new month's grid to exist before moving.

- Choosing a day closes the calendar through the component (closeOnDateSelect off): Bits UI closes it internally without calling onOpenChange, and not at all when the chosen day is already the value (preventDeselect).

- Week start from Intl.Locale weekInfo (Monday where the platform has none; Bits UI defaults to Sunday); weekday names short, narrow where the locale's short names are longer than four characters (Arabic).
- Locale passed with -u-ca-gregory (Gregorian whatever the locale's default calendar).

The calendar is rendered from the first opening, on the client only; the displayed month (placeholder) is a fixed date on the server and the current month once mounted, so that neither the server clock nor its time zone reaches the markup.
The month heading is a div, not a p, so that a page's own paragraph rules do not restyle it (seen on the review page).
